infl_ens.data.benchmarks¶

AI-safety benchmark loaders and learned trait-space construction.

This subpackage groups one module per benchmark used as a trait-space axis, plus a combined builder. Public surface:

  • BenchmarkSplit: uniform container of (prompt, score) records.

  • load_beavertails(): BeaverTails loader (harm axis).

  • load_halueval(): HaluEval loader (hallucination axis).

  • load_jbb_behaviors(): JBB-Behaviors loader (jailbreak axis).

  • load_toxicchat(): ToxicChat loader (legacy jailbreak axis).

  • load_ai4privacy(): AI4Privacy PII loader (privacy-density axis).

  • load_orbench(): OR-Bench loader (over-refusal axis).

  • load_prompt_injection(): prompt-injection loader (injection axis).

  • load_do_not_answer(): Do-Not-Answer loader (policy-violation axis).

  • build_safety_trait_space(): combined \(N\)-axis trait space.

  • LearnedAxis: a single scoring axis fit from labelled prompts.

  • BEAVERTAILS_CATEGORIES, HALUEVAL_TASKS, TOXICCHAT_SCORE_MODES, PII_SCORE_MODES, ORBENCH_CONFIGS: dataset taxonomy constants exposed for downstream filtering.

All loaders return BenchmarkSplit instances so downstream code (trait-space builders, trainers, evaluation scripts) handles every benchmark through one interface.

class infl_ens.data.benchmarks.BenchmarkSplit(name, prompts, scores, axis_name, responses=<factory>, metadata=<factory>)[source]¶

Bases: object

A loaded benchmark split in a single uniform shape.

Parameters:

  • name (str) – Benchmark identifier (e.g. 'beavertails', 'halueval-qa').

  • prompts (list[str]) – Raw user-facing prompts, length N. These are what the trait-space encoder will embed.

  • scores (numpy.ndarray) – Per-prompt benchmark axis score in [0, 1], length N. Higher means “more of the property the benchmark measures” (e.g. more harmful, more hallucinated).

  • responses (list[str]) – Optional per-prompt response strings (used at SFT time). Length N or empty.

  • axis_name (str) – Human-readable axis name, e.g. 'harm' or 'hallucination'.

  • metadata (dict) – Free-form metadata (split name, version, source URL).

class infl_ens.data.benchmarks.LearnedAxis(direction, lo, hi, name, residual_coef=None, residual_intercept=0.0, residual_lo=None, residual_hi=None)[source]¶

Bases: object

A unit-norm axis direction in embedding space.

Parameters:

  • direction (numpy.ndarray) – Unit vector in \(\mathbb{R}^D\), shape (D,).

  • lo (float) – Calibration low-end projection (maps to 0.0).

  • hi (float) – Calibration high-end projection (maps to 1.0).

  • name (str) – Human-readable axis name.

  • residual_coef (numpy.ndarray | None) – Optional coefficients for subtracting a linear prediction from previous calibrated coordinates.

  • residual_intercept (float) – Intercept for coordinate residualization.

  • residual_lo (float | None) – Calibration low endpoint for residualized scores.

  • residual_hi (float | None) – Calibration high endpoint for residualized scores.

project_raw_scores(embeddings)[source]¶

Project embeddings to the unclipped affine axis score.

The affine rescale keeps the calibration lo/hi orientation (lo maps to 0, hi maps to 1) but does not clip; the pipeline’s quantile normalizer must be fitted on these unclipped scores.

Parameters:

embeddings (numpy.ndarray) – Embedding matrix, shape (N, D).

Returns:

Per-row unclipped score, shape (N,).

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

project_scores(embeddings)[source]¶

Project a batch of embeddings to [0, 1] along this axis.

This method returns the independent base score. Projectors that use coordinate residualization apply the residual transform jointly across axes in _make_learned_projector().

Parameters:

embeddings (numpy.ndarray) – Embedding matrix, shape (N, D).

infl_ens.data.benchmarks.build_safety_trait_space(splits, encoder, *, n_grid=32, kde_bandwidth=None, threshold=0.5, calibration_corpus=None, coordinate_residualize=False, mode_alignment_weight=0.0, mode_alignment_weights=None, coordinate_stretch_gamma=1.0, coordinate_stretch_gammas=None, linear_transform=None, quantile_knots=1001)[source]¶

Construct a multi-axis TraitSpace from labelled benchmarks.

Thin wrapper around build_safety_trait_space_bundle() that returns only the TraitSpace.

Parameters:

  • splits (Sequence[BenchmarkSplit]) – One benchmark split per desired axis.

  • encoder (Callable[[Sequence[str]], numpy.ndarray]) – Sentence encoder used at fit and projection time.

  • n_grid (int) – Number of grid points per axis.

  • kde_bandwidth (float | None) – KDE bandwidth; None selects Scott’s rule.

  • threshold (float) – Score threshold for axis learning.

  • calibration_corpus (Sequence[str] | None) – Optional KDE calibration corpus.

  • coordinate_residualize (bool) – Whether to decorrelate later axes.

  • mode_alignment_weight (float) – Benchmark-mode blend weight.

  • mode_alignment_weights (dict[str, float] | None) – Per-axis mode blend overrides.

  • coordinate_stretch_gamma (float) – Default coordinate stretch exponent.

  • coordinate_stretch_gammas (dict[str, float] | None) – Per-axis stretch overrides.

  • linear_transform (FrozenLinearTransform | None) – Optional frozen standardize/whiten transform.

  • quantile_knots (int) – Quantile-grid size for the final normalizer.

Returns:

A TraitSpace of dimension L = len(splits).

Return type:

TraitSpace

Raises:

ValueError – If splits is empty.

infl_ens.data.benchmarks.load_ai4privacy(path, *, score_mode='density', english_only=True, max_records=None)[source]¶

Load AI4Privacy PII-masking data from a JSONL file or directory.

Parameters:

  • path (str | pathlib.Path) – Path to a .jsonl file, or to a directory containing the per-language shards (english_pii_43k.jsonl etc.). A directory is concatenated in lexicographic order.

  • score_mode (str) – Axis scoring mode. One of PII_SCORE_MODES. density (default) is the graded character-coverage fraction.

  • english_only (bool) – When path is a directory, restrict to files whose name contains "english". Ignored for single-file paths.

  • max_records (int | None) – Optional cap on the number of records to return.

Returns:

A BenchmarkSplit with axis_name='privacy'.

Return type:

BenchmarkSplit

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If path does not exist or no matching JSONL files are found under a directory.

  • ValueError – If score_mode is unknown or no records parse.

infl_ens.data.benchmarks.load_beavertails(path, *, categories=None, max_records=None)[source]¶

Load BeaverTails from a JSONL file or HuggingFace-cached directory.

Parameters:

  • path (str | pathlib.Path) – Path to a .jsonl file or to a directory containing train.jsonl / test.jsonl. A directory with several JSONL files is concatenated in lexicographic order.

  • categories (Iterable[str] | None) – Optional iterable of category names that should count toward the harm score. Defaults to all 14 categories.

  • max_records (int | None) – Optional cap on the number of records to return (post-filtering). Useful for fast smoke tests.

Returns:

A BenchmarkSplit with axis_name='harm'.

Return type:

BenchmarkSplit

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If path does not exist.

  • ValueError – If no records can be parsed.

  • max_records (int | None) – Optional cap on total records returned.

infl_ens.data.benchmarks.load_toxicchat(path, *, score_mode='jailbreaking', human_annotated_only=False, max_records=None)[source]¶

Load ToxicChat from a CSV file or a directory of CSV files.

Parameters:

  • path (str | pathlib.Path) – Path to a .csv file or to a directory containing one or more ToxicChat CSV files (e.g. toxic-chat_annotation_train.csv / toxic-chat_annotation_test.csv). A directory with several CSV files is concatenated in lexicographic order.

  • score_mode (str) – Which intrinsic label defines the axis. One of TOXICCHAT_SCORE_MODES. Defaults to 'jailbreaking', the axis most independent of the harm/hallucination axes.

  • human_annotated_only (bool) – If True, keep only rows whose human_annotation column is truthy (drops the auto-filtered non-toxic majority and yields a denser, higher-confidence split).

  • max_records (int | None) – Optional cap on the number of records to return (post-filtering). Useful for fast smoke tests.

Returns:

A BenchmarkSplit with axis_name='jailbreak'.

Return type:

BenchmarkSplit

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If path does not exist or no CSV files are found under a directory.

  • ValueError – If score_mode is unknown or no records parse.
